title: Derived evaluation with two targets of finite injective dimension
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use $R\operatorname{Hom}_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site and $\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}$ computed by a K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex] followed by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Suppose (i) $L$ and $M$ are each isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $R$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; (ii) $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)$ has finite Tor dimension, meaning there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every $R$-module $N$, $H^j(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$; and (iii) every good truncation $\tau_{\leq n}K$ (cohomology $H^j(K)$ for $j\leq n$ and zero otherwise) is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then the canonical derived evaluation morphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K,L,M$. The morphism is the transpose of evaluation followed by composition: $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to M$, pairing the first and third factors into $L$ and then evaluating into $M$, with the usual graded symmetries.

source.place: Tag 0A69, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-isomorphism-technical, with the canonical natural map of Tag 0A67, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate, and its construction from lemma-evaluate-and-more.

proof.text: Write $F(A)=T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}A$ and $G(A)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(A,L),M)$. By [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], these are exact functors and the evaluation-and-composition map $e_A:F(A)\to G(A)$ is a natural transformation compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles. This is exactly the map specified in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0A67 and 0A60; Tag 0A69 uses this map throughout

proof.text: Fix bounded injective complexes $J,I$ representing $L,M$ and integers $u,v$ with $J^r=0$ for $r>u$ and $I^r=0$ for $r<v$. They are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], clause (2). In particular $L$ is bounded below, since $J$ is bounded. For each integer $n$ take the standard truncation triangle $A_n=\tau_{\le n}K\to K\to E_n=\tau_{\ge n+1}K\to A_n[1]$, using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] and [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], clause (1). Its tail has a representative $B_n$ with $B_n^r=0$ for $r<n+1$, by the representative characterization in the standard t-structure.

source.place: Tag 0A69, truncation triangle; derived.tex Remark Tag 08J5; bounded injective representatives as in Section Injective dimension

proof.text: Hypothesis (iii) says $A_n$ is pseudo-coherent for every $n$. Apply [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-pseudocoherent] with $K=A_n$, the bounded-below object $L$ of Step 2 and the finite-injective-dimension object $M$ of hypothesis (i). Thus $e_{A_n}$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

Fix once and for all the Tor-amplitude interval $[a,b]$ of hypothesis (ii). By [lem-pc-module-tor-amplitude-flat-model], $T$ has a bounded flat representative $P$ with terms supported in $[a,b]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Hence $F(E_n)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R B_n)$. By the total tensor formula [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], a nonzero summand in degree $r$ requires indices $i\ge a$, $j\ge n+1$ and $i+j=r$. Thus this representative, and its cohomology, vanish in degrees $r<n+1+a$. The integer $a$ does not depend on $n$.

The Hom-complex formula in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], using the K-injective representatives from Step 2, computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_n,L)$ by $C_n=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(B_n,J)$. Its degree-$s$ factors are $\operatorname{Hom}_R(B_n^r,J^{r+s})$. If such a factor is nonzero then $r\ge n+1$ and $r+s\le u$, so $s\le u-n-1$. Next $G(E_n)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(C_n,I)$. A nonzero degree-$t$ factor requires $s\le u-n-1$ and $s+t\ge v$, whence $t\ge n+1+v-u$. Thus $G(E_n)$ has no cohomology below that bound. Set $c=\max(-a,u-v)$, independent of $n$. Steps 4 and 5 show that both tails have zero cohomology in every degree $\le n-c$.

source.place: Tag 0A69, double-Hom tail; the Hom-complex definition preceding Tag 0A65

proof.text: By [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map], applying $F,G,e$ to the triangle of Step 2 gives two distinguished triangles and a commuting comparison. Fix a degree $d$ and choose $n\ge d+c$. Both tail objects have zero $H^{d-1}$ and $H^d$. In the exact cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], the maps $H^d(F(A_n))\to H^d(F(K))$ and $H^d(G(A_n))\to H^d(G(K))$ are therefore isomorphisms: each has zero term immediately before its source and after its target. The comparison square commutes by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder], so $H^d(e_K)$ is the conjugate of the isomorphism $H^d(e_{A_n})$ of Step 3 by these horizontal isomorphisms. This holds for every integer $d$. The cohomology criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives that $e_K$ is an isomorphism. It is the same canonical map for all choices of $n$, so its naturality in $K,L,M$ is the naturality in Step 1.
